b7143338e322.title: folio-assistant-sci
b7143338e322.content: Scientific source material used by folios that formalise mathematics, and the methodologies for formalising it in Lean that this layer adopts from that material.

fc6997ca7ca0.title: What this layer holds
fc6997ca7ca0.content: . | The paper content adapter (content-adapters/, adapters/paper/): how a paper folio’s blocks become LaTeX, PDF and HTML, and how the suggest editor checks paper math. | Skills (skills/): authoring mathematics in Markdown and LaTeX, Lean formalisation and proof review, the proof, rendering and compute audits, and the integration watchers that run them on every change. | Tools (tools/): one node per command a skill or process calls, such as lean-build, lean-cache, latex-preflight, paper-latex-build and tex-snippet-validate, each with its inputs and outputs. | Library and methodologies (library/, methodologies/): the papers this layer reads, and the Lean formalisation methods adopted from three of them. | .

17ef79a2665b.title: Processes
17ef79a2665b.content: Four BPMN processes say who does what: . | Authoring a paper. The author (a person) plans the paper. The authoring agent seeds the work plan, scaffolds the folio repository and authors blocks. The Lean toolchain role formalises claims in Lean, and the build pipeline validates the folio and renders the PDF and HTML. | Publish a folio’s Lean render. The doc-gen4 HTML of a folio’s Lean package, staged under its site with the harness navbar and rail. | Formalized Scientific Publication Authoring. One mathematical result as a triple (narrative statement, narrative proof, Lean), checked mechanically and then by blind two-way translation and a semantic-equivalence judge. See section 10 below. | Atomic mass drift check. Whether AtomicMass.lean still matches its data table. | . Each process has a generated checklist beside it for an agent that walks the steps by hand.

a924d40373a3.title: Guides
a924d40373a3.content: The guide walks the authoring process end to end, from planning the paper to publishing it. | Writing a paper with folio-assistant | .

9345936800f0.title: A survey: agentic authoring of formalized publications
9345936800f0.content: For newcomers: what folio-assistant does, how a document is started, which checks run, which data models it uses, and how this layer extends it to machine-checked mathematics.

c8caa99f6887.title: 1. The problem
c8caa99f6887.content: A large language model can draft text quickly. It can also state a false result fluently, cite a paper that says something else, or let two chapters drift apart. For policy guidance this is a quality problem. For mathematics it is fatal, because a published proof is a claim that anyone may check. folio-assistant treats a publication as a knowledge graph of small, typed units rather than as one long file. Every unit has a declared kind, declared dependencies and a set of checks. Some checks are programs. Others are agents that read the unit without seeing who wrote it. The author, human or agent, works inside that graph, and the graph refuses changes that break it.

2fa814017906.title: 2. The architecture in one picture
2fa814017906.content: The system is a stack of layers. Each may import from the layers below it and never from the layers above. The direction is checked (bun run cat check:partition:edges). | layer | repository | what it owns | . | bootstrap | litlfred/bootstrap | what an agent reads before anything is installed | . | harness | litlfred/cat-harness, cat-harness-tools | skills, BPMN processes, the work plan (beans), the MCP server, QA sidecars | . | core | litlfred/folio-assistant-core | the content-object model, block kinds, the document adapter, the library and its catalogue | . | science (this layer) | litlfred/folio-assistant-sci | the paper adapter: Lean-bearing block kinds, LaTeX rendering, witnesses | . | domain | smart-base, fhir-harness, … | WHO SMART Guidelines, FHIR Implementation Guides | . The index repository litlfred/folio-assistant pins one commit of each layer, so a folio always validates against a known platform. Three ideas run through every layer. | Processes are executable, not illustrations. Each workflow is a BPMN 2.0 diagram under processes/, and each task in it names the skill an agent follows to perform it. | Skills are the instructions. A skill is a Markdown file with front matter. An agent asks the graph for the skill list (skill_list, skill_fetch) rather than reading a hard-coded list. | Work is recorded. An active folio keeps its work plan as beans, so a later agent can pick up what an earlier one left. | .

502a13f3024a.title: 3. Starting a document in a new, empty repository
502a13f3024a.content: The full guide is Writing a document. In short: . git init git submodule add https://github.com/litlfred/folio-assistant.git folio-assistant (cd folio-assistant && bun install) bun run folio-assistant/scripts/init-folio.ts \ --type document \ --title "My Document" \ --author "A. Author" . Use --type paper for a mathematics paper (this needs the science layer). If your agent already has a folio-assistant MCP server connected, you can instead ask it in plain words to initialise a document folio in the repository. After scaffolding, the usual loop is: . | Plan. Ask the agent for the chapter and section skeleton (skill document-structure). It writes the chapter manifests. | Ingest sources. Drop PDFs into uploads/. The agent turns each into a library entry (section 7). | Author. The agent writes blocks one at a time: a manifest, a narrative file and, for formal kinds, a Lean file. | Validate. Mechanical checks run on every change; agentic checks run on the changed blocks and their dependents (section 5). | Review and publish. Each change set becomes one pull request with a staging preview. A person merges. | .

89ad4028fe2d.title: 4. The data models
89ad4028fe2d.content: | model | what it describes | where | . | block | one atomic unit: a definition, a theorem, a recommendation, a figure, a paragraph of prose | block-kinds/*.json in core, plus the formal kinds (definition, theorem, lemma, …) in this layer | . | chapter / paper manifest | the ordered tree of sections over block references | <chapter>/<chapter>.ts in each folio | . | uses[] graph | each block’s immediate dependencies; the transitive graph is walked, never written | the block manifest | . | QA sidecar | per-block verdicts of every check, keyed to hashes of the files they read, so a stale verdict is detectable | <block>.qa.json (schema block-qa/v1) | . | library entry | an ingested source: PDF, structure, section text, extracted claims | library/<doc-id>/ | . | Dublin Core record, catalogue, materialization | what the source says about itself, which collection it is in, and whether the bytes are held here | schemas/dublin-core.ts, catalogue.ts, materialization.ts | . | change set | what changed between two refs, block by block | schemas/changeset.ts | . | review comment | a reviewer’s comment on one block, as a todo with a closed lifecycle | schemas/review-comment.ts | . | witness | the recorded output of a computation, with the hash of the script that produced it | *.witness.json (section 8) | . | bibliography | one CSL-JSON file per reference; BibTeX is generated from it | references/<id>.json in each folio | . A block’s file triple shares one root name: . definition-of-x.ts typed manifest: kind, label, uses[], lean reference definition-of-x.md narrative statement and proof, in Markdown with TeX definition-of-x.lean formal statement and proof (formal kinds only) .

2be821eb47c6.title: 5. Two kinds of validation: mechanical and agentic
2be821eb47c6.content: Mechanical checks are programs. They are cheap, deterministic and run on every change. Examples: . | schema validation of every manifest (Zod); | every uses[] reference and cross-reference resolves; | every defined term is declared once and marked at every use; | the rendered LaTeX parses, and the math in Markdown renders; | Lean compiles, and no sorry lacks a bibliographic citation; | a vacuity audit flags theorems that conclude True, empty conjecture classes and similar ways of passing a check without asserting anything; | every citation key exists and every DOI resolves; | witness staleness: a recorded number is flagged when the script that produced it changes. | . Agentic checks are performed by agents following a skill, because the question needs judgement. Examples: . | semantic equivalence between a Lean statement and its narrative statement (section 6); | a devil’s-advocate review that builds the strongest case that a block is wrong; | scholarly voice, definition clarity and expository order; | whether a cited source actually supports the sentence citing it. | . The two kinds meet in the same QA sidecar. An agentic verdict is recorded with the hashes of the files it read, so it goes stale the moment one of them changes, exactly like a mechanical verdict. An agent cannot clear its own finding: findings are cleared by a fresh verdict, by a different reviewer, or by a person.

40b9a378d908.title: 6. Mathematical results as a triple
40b9a378d908.content: In this layer, a mathematical result is not one object but three: . | part | file | checked by | . | narrative statement | the statement paragraph of <block>.md | agent reading, render check | . | narrative proof | the proof section of <block>.md | agent reading, proof-gap audit | . | formal statement and proof | <block>.lean | the Lean kernel | . The Lean kernel guarantees only that the formal proof proves the formal statement. It says nothing about whether that formal statement is the theorem the narrative claims. A formal statement can be weaker, can quietly assume its conclusion, or can be about a different object with the same name. The triple is therefore validated by blind, two-way agentic translation: . | One agent reads only the Lean statement and writes what it says in mathematical prose, without seeing the narrative. | A second agent reads only the narrative statement and writes what a formal statement of it must assert, without seeing the Lean. | A third agent judges semantic equivalence of each translation against the other side’s original: same hypotheses, same quantifier order, same conclusion, same objects. | . Disagreement in either direction is a finding. The narrative proof is checked against the Lean proof in the same blind way for its logical skeleton, so that the human-readable argument and the formal one are the same argument, not merely two routes to the same label. Three further rules keep the triple honest: . | an unproved step is stated with sorry and a citation, never hidden; | a result that depends on a conjecture either becomes a conjecture or takes the conjecture as an explicit hypothesis, visible in the Lean signature; | a sorry-free proof is not evidence that the statement is the right one, so equivalence is checked even when Lean is green. | . When a paper is published, every formal block links to its declaration in the rendered Lean library (the doc-gen4 HTML that the skill lean-html-docs builds and stages beside the paper’s own site), so a reader can move from the sentence to the checked code in one click.

dc64fb0b60b1.title: 7. The library: open-access sources inside the knowledge graph
dc64fb0b60b1.content: Sources are not a bibliography at the end. They are nodes of the graph. An open-access paper, book or guideline dropped into uploads/ is ingested (processes under processes/library/) into library/<doc-id>/: . | file | holds | . | the PDF | the bytes, with their checksum | . | structure.json | metadata, table of contents, section index | . | sections/*.md | the text of each section, searchable by grep | . | candidates.json | extracted definitions, theorems and claims, as proposals only | . | a Dublin Core record | what the source says about itself | . The library serves three purposes. | Reference validation. A citation is checked against the held text, not only against its metadata. An agent can confirm that the cited section says what the citing sentence claims. | Prior-work search. Before an agent declares a question open, it searches the library as well as the folio. Many “open” results are already settled in a paper the project holds. | Formalizing existing papers. Extracted statements from a held paper can be turned into Lean statements, with the paper’s narrative as the reference side of the triple in section 6. This lets a folio cross-reference results from the literature at the formal level, not only by citation. | . A source that cannot be held (licence, size) is recorded as referenced, with no bytes. Its state is declared, never assumed (see the three materialization states in README.md).

95e8ee05adac.title: 8. Witnesses: binding computation to mathematics
95e8ee05adac.content: Some results need computation: a numerical value, an enumeration, a counterexample search. A computation in a paper folio writes a witness file, which records: . | the values computed, serialized at a declared precision; | the hash of the producing script, so the witness goes stale when the script changes; | the environment and inputs it ran with. | . A block that quotes a number names its witness, and the number in the prose is read from it rather than typed by hand. This gives a chain from the narrative, through the witness, to the script that produced it, and where possible to a Lean statement that pins the same identity exactly. A computation suggests; a Lean proof establishes. A witness is never cited as the proof of a theorem.

a29eb5573301.title: 9. Keeping mathematics and measurement apart
a29eb5573301.content: A scientific paper often contains both theorems and comparisons with experiment. The two must not mix. | Formal blocks contain no empirical inputs. No measured constant may enter a Lean statement or a narrative proof as a hypothesis. | Comparison is a separate place. The point where a model quantity is set against a measured one (for example a CODATA value) is a marked comparison block, and that is where the empirical claim lives. | Fitting is visible. A quantity chosen to match data, including choosing one object from a list because it matches, is labelled as a fit and is never presented as a derivation. | Approximate equalities say so. A computed value compared with measurement uses ≈, not =. | .

a17dccce11ac.title: 10. The process: Formalized Scientific Publication Authoring
a17dccce11ac.content: The diagram processes/content/formalized-publication-authoring.bpmn is this layer’s process for one mathematical result, in five lanes: the author, the authoring agent, the Lean toolchain, the build pipeline (mechanical checks) and the independent reviewers. Each task names the skill an agent follows to perform it. | The author states the intended result and its sources. | The agent searches the folio and the library for prior work. A result already proved there is cited, and the process ends. | The agent drafts the triple: narrative statement, narrative proof, Lean. | The Lean toolchain compiles the block and reports sorry and axioms; the build pipeline runs the mechanical checks: schema, references, render, vacuity, witnesses. | In parallel, one independent agent translates the Lean to prose without the narrative, and another translates the narrative to a formal claim without the Lean. A judge compares both ways, and an adversarial reviewer makes the strongest case that the block is wrong. | Any finding returns the block to the agent. If the result cannot be closed, it is kept as a conjecture or as a stated, cited gap. | When every check is green, the change set goes to a pull request, and the author merges. | . It complements Authoring a paper, which covers the paper as a whole (planning, the work plan, scaffolding, rendering); this process is the loop each formal block goes through inside it.

8e5cc96b9fe4.title: 11. From guideline authoring to scientific authoring
8e5cc96b9fe4.content: The same machinery was first built for WHO SMART Guidelines, where a recommendation in a health-policy document must trace to its evidence, and an implementation guide must stay consistent with the guideline it implements. The generalisation is direct: . | SMART Guidelines | scientific publication | . | recommendation | theorem, proposition, definition | . | evidence profile | narrative proof and cited sources | . | computable artefact (FHIR, CQL, DMN) | Lean formalization | . | consistency of guideline and implementation | semantic equivalence of narrative and Lean | . | test data and conformance checks | witnesses and their producing scripts | . | public comment on a draft | contributor feedback and pull-request review | . In both cases the method is the same: break the publication into typed units, give each unit a machine form and a human form, check that the two say the same thing, and keep a record that shows which checks ran on which version.

abead14c0bec.title: 12. Worked example and licence
abead14c0bec.content: Worked example. litlfred/qou, a mathematics paper, was written with folio-assistant-sci on top of this layer. It uses every mechanism above: block triples, a Lean library, witnesses, an ingested library of several hundred papers, and blind equivalence review. Licence. d8efd7040ad5.title: Tutorial — writing a paper with folio-assistant
d8efd7040ad5.content: TR… . On this page . | The end-to-end workflow | Before you start | Step 1 — Plan the paper | Step 2 — Scaffold the repository . | Required .gitignore baseline | . | Step 3 — Author the content | Step 4 — Formalize in Lean | Step 5 — Validate | Step 6 — Render | Step 7 — Review & feedback | Step 8 — Publish | What you end up with | Where to go deeper | . This page is generated from docs/source/guides-writing-a-paper/ — each section below links to its own source. ✎ Edit QA… TR… . This tutorial walks through authoring a rigorous scientific paper with an LLM driving folio-assistant: the agent plans the paper, drafts blocks, formalizes theorems in Lean 4, renders LaTeX, and publishes — while you steer. It uses a small running example, “A note on the harmonic series”, to illustrate the workflow.

cb55e02ac386.title: The end-to-end workflow
cb55e02ac386.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… KG… . BPMN 2.0 source · full-size SVG . Every step is something the LLM does for you by calling folio-assistant’s MCP tools — you converse in natural language and approve the work. Approve is literal: steps 3–5 are a loop, and the assistant’s edit is a proposal until you have seen the validation findings and accepted it. The publication workflow models that gate, and the review and release that follow, as BPMN swimlane diagrams.

cbaf4e806d82.title: Before you start
cbaf4e806d82.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… . | Install folio-assistant and run bun run cat check-deps. For papers you want bun, latexmk/texlive, and Lean (elan). | Connect your LLM harness (Claude Code, Antigravity, …) so the agent has the MCP tools. | Create an (empty) content repository for your paper and add a <name>.config.json with "contentType": "paper". | .

24e92417bbc3.title: Step 1 — Plan the paper
24e92417bbc3.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… . Start by asking the agent to load the planning skill and propose a structure. Behind the scenes it calls skill_fetch content-plan. You: I want to write a short paper, “A note on the harmonic series”. It should define the partial sums, state and prove that the series diverges, and include one worked example. Plan it out. Assistant: (loads content-plan) Here’s a proposed plan: . | prose — Introduction & motivation | definition def:harmonic-partial-sum — the partial sum $H_n$ | theorem thm:harmonic-diverges — $H_n \to \infty$ | proof prf:harmonic-diverges — Oresme’s grouping argument | example ex:H4 — compute $H_4$ | . The definition and theorem will get Lean counterparts. Shall I scaffold the repo and create these blocks as drafts? . You: Yes, go ahead. This is also where you’d open work-plan items so the plan survives across sessions: . beans create "Draft harmonic-series paper: blocks + Lean" beans <id> --status in-progress .

5a0cb12a4dfb.title: Step 2 — Scaffold the repository
5a0cb12a4dfb.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… . The agent creates the block files and a main.tex, then confirms with content_list. Assistant: (creates blocks, calls content_list) Scaffolded 5 blocks under content/harmonic-series/. Current artifacts: . content/harmonic-series/ ├── 00-intro.prose.md ├── 10-def-partial-sum.definition.md ├── 20-thm-diverges.theorem.md ├── 21-prf-diverges.proof.md └── 30-ex-h4.example.md . Each block carries typed front-matter validated against the content-object model. A definition block, for example: . --- kind: definition id: def:harmonic-partial-sum title: Harmonic partial sum lean: HarmonicSeries.partialSum --- For $n \ge 1$, the *$n$-th harmonic partial sum* is $$ H_n = \sum_{k=1}^{n} \frac{1}{k}. $$ . Required .gitignore baseline . ✎ Edit QA… TR… . Every new folio repository starts with these entries. Agent sandboxes accumulate scratch directories as untracked state, and a single git add -A then commits all of it under a message describing something else. # Agent scratch state — transient tooling state, never repository content. # Leading slash = root-level only. Keep it (see the warning below). /.agents/ /amalgamated_done/ /amalgamated_input/ /_deprecated/ /scratch/ .claude/worktrees/ # Python bytecode __pycache__/ *.py[cod] . Keep the leading slashes. A gitignore pattern with no internal slash matches at every directory depth, not just the root: unanchored, _deprecated/ would also catch a nested archive such as computations/_deprecated/, and scratch/ every content/**/scratch/. An ignore rule never untracks a file, but any new file under such a path is skipped by git add with no error and no output. If your folio keeps a nested archive or scratch area under one of these names, the anchored form keeps it committable. Two deliberate exclusions: . | beans/ stays tracked. It is the durable, cross-session work plan; a sibling agent has to be able to read it. Bean duplication is prevented by the create-guard of the todo-manager skill, not by ignoring the directory. | Any directory your folio documents as a real pipeline stays tracked — in qou, uploads/ is the document-intake stage and belongs in git. Check your own AGENTS.md §Project structure before adding a path to this list: if it is documented there, it is content, not scratch. | .

49ba744dd16f.title: Step 3 — Author the content
49ba744dd16f.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… . Ask the agent to draft prose and statements; review and refine conversationally. You: Draft the introduction and the divergence theorem statement. Assistant: (loads content-author, edits the blocks) Done. The theorem reads: “The sequence $(H_n)$ is unbounded; equivalently $\sum 1/k$ diverges.” I kept the statement Lean-friendly so it maps cleanly to Filter.Tendsto. A mock of the chat-driven authoring session: .

622c9040b41b.title: Step 4 — Formalize in Lean
622c9040b41b.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… . Now the agent sets up Lean and formalizes the definition and theorem, calling lean_setup, lean_build, and lean_check. You: Formalize the definition and theorem in Lean and make it build. Assistant: (loads lean-formalization; calls lean_setup) Toolchain ready (Lean 4.16.0). I added: . namespace HarmonicSeries def partialSum (n : ℕ) : ℝ := ∑ k ∈ Finset.range n, 1 / (k + 1 : ℝ) theorem diverges : ¬ ∃ B, ∀ n, partialSum n ≤ B := by sorry -- Ref: [oresme] grouping argument . (calls lean_build) Build is green with 1 sorry remaining. (calls lean_status) Proof coverage: 1/2 blocks fully proved. You: Discharge the sorry using the grouping bound. dbe5d986c098.title: Step 5 — Validate
dbe5d986c098.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… . Validation checks every block against its schema and the project’s constraint rules (label prefixes, required Lean links, citation resolution, …). You: Validate the whole paper. Assistant: (calls content_validate) All 5 blocks valid. Constraints: def: block has its required Lean link ✓, theorem has a proof block ✓, example references a defined symbol ✓.

86518370c64f.title: Step 6 — Render
86518370c64f.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… . The agent renders a PDF (and/or HTML) with the paper adapter. You: Render the PDF and show me a preview. Assistant: (calls paper_render_pdf, then paper_preview) Rendered harmonic-series.pdf (3 pages). Preview below. You can set rendering preferences (engine, scope, math renderer) via the paper_preferences tool: . You: Use lualatex and render only the theorem section next time. ba4449d4c2bc.title: Step 7 — Review & feedback
ba4449d4c2bc.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… . Reviewer feedback is captured in the feedback store and routed back into the authoring loop (content-review / content-feedback). You: A reviewer says the example should also show $H_8$. Log it and address it. Assistant: (records feedback, edits ex:H4 → adds $H_8$, re-validates, re-renders) Done; feedback item resolved.

3e9795f01f5d.title: Step 8 — Publish
3e9795f01f5d.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… . Finally, publish the rendered artifacts. In CI this is the publish workflow; locally the agent runs content_build and the render tools, then commits. You: Publish it. Assistant: (loads content-publish, content_build, commits + pushes) Published. PDF, HTML, and the Lean blueprint are built; the work-plan item is marked resolved. beans <id> --status resolved .
